nodes.label: OpenAPI Spec as Source of Truth
nodes.norm_label: openapi spec as source of truth

nodes.label: Spec-First Without a Behavioral Contract
nodes.rationale: The legacy TS test suite died with the wipe, so rather than chasing v5's behavioral-parity strategy, each service's openapi.yaml becomes the sole contract; behavioral regressions versus the old API are accepted by design since no production consumers depend on it.

nodes.label: Deliberately Avoided Versioning Practices
nodes.rationale: Per-consumer version negotiation headers are overkill while all consumers are first-party frontends; long-lived public SDKs are unnecessary because packages/contracts regenerates from the aggregate spec on every build, keeping clients in sync automatically.

nodes.label: /api/v1 Frozen Contract
nodes.rationale: Freezing request/response shapes for any route shipped in /api/v1 until a minor deprecation window prevents silent breaking changes for first-party frontend consumers; additive changes (new optional fields, routes, permissions) are exempt so iteration is not blocked.

nodes.label: PR Checklist
nodes.rationale: Enforcing conventional commits, migration-pair-per-column, spec-first API changes, and typed-client-only fetch keeps commit history, schema history, and the API contract from drifting out of sync.

nodes.label: JWT Verified Once At Edge
nodes.rationale: Verifying JWTs once at the gateway edge and forwarding identity bound by an internal secret avoids redundant per-service verification cost and centralizes the trust boundary.

nodes.label: Migration Execution Model (k8s Job vs boot-time)
nodes.norm_label: migration execution model (k8s job vs boot-time)

nodes.label: ADR-0001: Fresh-build Pivot
nodes.rationale: The owner directed a full pivot from a TypeScript/Express/Sequelize/Socket.IO API to Go microservices behind a Go gateway with React microfrontends in the same monorepo; the old codebase was deleted outright (recoverable via git history) rather than frozen for parity.

nodes.label: GORM Replaces sqlc/pgx-direct
nodes.rationale: Reversal of the pre-wipe decision: velocity and ecosystem win at this scale, and reflection overhead is accepted as the trade-off.

nodes.label: Schema-per-Service Decision
nodes.rationale: One Postgres cluster with schema-per-service (auth/users/rbac/audit), per-service creds scoped to their own schema, and zero cross-schema writes keeps future extraction cheap while avoiding N-database operational overhead now; lifecycle changes ride Redis Streams events instead of direct writes.

nodes.label: Expand/Contract Zero-Downtime Migration
nodes.rationale: Multi-replica rolling deploys run old and new pod binaries side by side, so a migration must never break the previous binary: add nullable/expand first, deploy dual-write code, only then contract (enforce NOT NULL, drop old columns) in a later migration.

nodes.label: Hardening Extras Found During Execution
nodes.rationale: The resilience drill uncovered that auth trusted a bearer header the gateway had already stripped; the fix moved auth to rely on gateway-forwarded identity headers instead, closing a trust-boundary gap.

nodes.label: CSRF Mitigation by Construction
nodes.rationale: CSRF exposure is bounded structurally rather than via CSRF tokens: cookie-bearing endpoints are POST-only, handlers decode JSON only so forged form posts fail binding, SameSite=Lax blocks cross-site POST navigation, and the access token is never stored in a cookie so forged top-level requests cannot authorize API calls.

nodes.label: Memory Access Token / httpOnly Refresh Cookie Split
nodes.norm_label: memory access token / httponly refresh cookie split
nodes.rationale: Access tokens live only in memory so XSS cannot read them via storage APIs; refresh tokens live in an httpOnly cookie so JavaScript cannot exfiltrate them; rotation on every use plus whole-family kill on replay bounds the blast radius of a stolen refresh token.
